step1.title: The Shipper Posts a Job
step1.sub: Every shipment starts the same way — from the shipper app.

1.title: Describe your cargo
1.desc: Enter the item, quantity (in quintals), pickup and destination locations, and your preferred dates.

2.title: Choose your vehicle

ind.title: Individual Drivers

ind.b1: Up to 5 bids per vehicle slot
ind.b2: You choose the driver per slot

comp.title: Transport Companies
comp.desc: Your job becomes a company batch. Verified companies bid on the whole batch; one bid per company; they assign fleet & drivers.
comp.b1: One bid per company for the batch
comp.b3: Great for big fleets & full convoys

step3.title: Then the Job Flows
step3.sub: Individual, company, and queue flows — plus street pickup and call center help when you need them.

ind.title: Individual Driver Bidding
ind.sub: For jobs of 10 or fewer vehicles. Up to 5 drivers bid per slot; you pick the winner.

comp.title: Company Batch Bidding
comp.sub: For jobs of more than 10 vehicles. Companies bid on the batch; you accept one and they assign the fleet.

queue.title: Queue Dispatch at Loading Places
queue.sub: Ports, customs, factories, and depots run a fair FIFO line — or open orders for bidding.

street.title: Take From Street
street.sub: For drivers who find a shipper on the road without the app. Perfect for street-side pickups and walk-in customers.

1.title: Drivers Are Matched
1.desc: Individual drivers near your pickup point are invited to your job — up to 5 verified drivers are invited per vehicle slot. Drivers at the loading-place queue get priority.

2.title: Drivers Submit Bids
2.desc: Each driver reviews your load and submits their best price for the slot. You see every bid, driver rating, and vehicle detail in real time.

3.title: You Select the Driver
3.desc: Compare prices and ratings and pick the best driver for each vehicle slot. Selected drivers confirm and prepare for pickup.

4.title: Track & Deliver
4.desc: The driver loads and starts the journey — you follow live GPS until delivery. Pay and rate at the end.

1.title: Companies See the Batch
1.desc: Transport companies with large fleets see your full batch — the total number of vehicles needed, route, cargo, and timeline. They place one bid for the entire batch.

2.title: Companies Bid
2.desc: Multiple verified companies compete with a price per vehicle. You compare bids and company ratings side by side.

3.title: You Accept a Company Bid
3.desc: Choose the company that best fits your budget and needs. Once accepted, the job is locked to them.

4.title: Company Assigns Drivers
4.desc: The company assigns its drivers and vehicles to every slot — automatically or manually through their portal. Each assigned driver confirms the assignment.

5.title: Track Every Slot
5.desc: Follow each assigned truck with live GPS from loading to delivery. Payment and rating happen per delivered slot.

1.title: Order Enters the Queue
1.desc: A job linked to a loading place (port, customs, factory, cement plant, depot) enters that site's dispatch queue. Queue staff can create it on your behalf.

2.title: Drivers Check In (FIFO)
2.desc: Drivers check in at the loading place and join a first-in-first-out line for their vehicle type. The front waiting driver is offered the order.

3.title: Offer, Accept or Timeout
3.desc: The driver has a short window to accept. If they decline or time out, the order moves to the next driver in line. Too many refusals sends a driver to the back.

4.title: Open for Bidding
4.desc: Queue staff can open an order for bidding instead of FIFO — up to 5 drivers bid per vehicle slot. You or the queue staff pick the winning bid.

5.title: Load, Track & Complete
5.desc: The winning driver loads, heads to your destination, and you track the full journey to completion.

1.title: Driver Meets Shipper
1.desc: Driver finds a shipper at a loading zone, marketplace, or on the road who needs transport but does not have the app.

2.title: Quick Registration
2.desc: Driver opens the app and enters the shipper's phone number, cargo details, and pickup/destination locations.

3.title: Instant SMS Confirmation
3.desc: The system creates accounts for both parties. The shipper receives SMS with driver details, vehicle info, and a tracking link.

4.title: Journey Begins
4.desc: The journey starts immediately with GPS tracking active. No bidding phase required.

1.title: Call DTC Hotline
1.desc: Shipper calls the DTC call center hotline for phone-based booking assistance.

2.title: Operator Collects Details
2.desc: An operator collects all shipment information: origin, destination, item description, quantity, and vehicle type preference.

3.title: Request Created
3.desc: The operator creates the request in the system on behalf of the shipper. The request enters the normal bid-matching flow.

4.title: SMS Updates
4.desc: The shipper receives SMS updates on driver assignment, bid acceptance, and journey progress.

hero.title: Frequently Asked Questions
hero.sub: Find answers to common questions about shipping, driver registration, pricing, tracking, and more.

q1.q: How do I post a shipment request?
q1.a: Download the DTC app, register with your phone number, and verify via OTP. Then tap 'Post Shipment' and enter your pickup location, destination, cargo details (item name, quantity in quintals), vehicle type needed, and preferred dates. You can set a budget or let drivers bid freely.

q2.q: How long does it take to get matched with a driver?
q2.a: Our system automatically finds verified drivers within approximately 1 km of your pickup location. Drivers are notified instantly and can place bids within minutes. Most shippers receive their first bid within 5-10 minutes.

q3.q: Can I request multiple vehicles at once?
q3.a: Yes! You can create a batch request for multiple vehicles in one submission. This is useful for large shipments that need more than one truck.

q4.q: What if no drivers bid on my shipment?
q4.a: If no drivers bid within a reasonable time, try adjusting your budget, expanding the vehicle type options, or reposting at a different time. You can also call our support center for assistance.

q5.q: Can I cancel my shipment request?
q5.a: Yes, you can cancel before the journey starts. All matched drivers will be notified. However, cancellations are tracked and excessive cancellations may affect your account standing.

q1.q: What documents do I need to register as a driver?
q1.a: Required documents: Driver's License (with expiration date and file number), Vehicle Registration/Librea (with file number), and Profile Photo. Optional but recommended: Insurance Document, Tax Identification Number, National ID, and Delegation of Vehicle Use.

q2.q: How long does the verification process take?
q2.a: Typically 24-48 hours after you submit all required documents. Our admin team reviews each submission carefully. You'll be notified when your account is approved.

q3.a: We support eight vehicle classes, from Light Trucks (up to 35 quintals) and Medium Trucks (up to 50 or 100 quintals) to Heavy Trucks (125–175 quintals), Extra Heavy Trucks (176–250 quintals), and multi-container rigs for 40ft ISO containers (up to 400 quintals). Each vehicle must be registered with its license plate, color, and type.

q4.q: Do I need to own the vehicle?
q4.a: You can drive a vehicle you own or one that's been delegated to you. If it's not your vehicle, you'll need a Delegation of Vehicle Use document from the owner.

q5.q: What happens if my documents expire?
q5.a: The platform tracks document expiration dates. You'll receive alerts before expiration. If a document expires, your status will change to inactive until you upload the renewed document.

q1.q: How is the shipping price determined?
q1.a: Prices are determined through competitive bidding. When you post a shipment, drivers submit their proposed prices. You can set a budget or leave it open. Choose the best offer based on price, driver ratings, and vehicle type.

q2.q: Are there any fees for shippers?
q2.a: No, shippers do not pay any platform fees. You only pay the agreed shipping cost directly to the driver. Driver fees are being launched at zero — the platform is free during the launch period.

q3.a: DTC is currently free — no commission is charged yet. We are launching with a free period and will introduce a transparent commission structure in the future. Any changes will be announced clearly.

q4.a: We accept Cash on Delivery, Bank Transfer (CBE, Dashen, and others), and Telebirr/Mobile Money. Choose the method that works best for you.

q5.q: What are the driver subscription plans?
q5.a: Free Trial (1 month, for new drivers), Monthly (700 ETB), Quarterly (1,800 ETB, save 300 ETB), and Annual (6,000 ETB, save 2,400 ETB). Drivers need an active subscription to receive shipment requests.

q1.q: How do I track my shipment?
q1.a: Once the driver starts the journey, you'll see a live map in the app showing the truck's real-time location. GPS tracking is continuous from pickup to delivery.

q2.q: What happens when my cargo arrives?
q2.a: The driver taps 'Complete Journey' when they arrive at the destination. You'll receive a notification to confirm delivery. After confirmation, you can rate the driver and make payment.

q3.q: What if there's a problem during delivery?
q3.a: Contact our 24/7 support center immediately. You can report issues through the app or by calling. Our admin team can intervene, cancel journeys, or help resolve disputes.

q4.q: Can I communicate with the driver?
q4.a: Yes, once a driver is assigned to your shipment, you can see their contact information in the app and coordinate directly for pickup details.

q1.a: Every driver must submit a valid Driver's License, Vehicle Registration (Librea), and Profile Photo. Documents are reviewed by our admin team. Drivers must also maintain an active subscription and good standing.

q2.a: After every journey, both shipper and driver rate each other (1-5 stars) with optional comments. Ratings help build trust and help others make informed decisions.

q3.q: What happens if a driver has bad ratings?
q3.a: Drivers with consistently poor ratings or violations (late arrival, rude behavior, cancellations) accumulate delinquency points. Too many points result in automatic temporary or permanent bans.

q4.a: Yes. All passwords and OTPs are hashed using industry-standard encryption. API communication is secured via token-based authentication (JWT). We only share your information with matched drivers during active journeys.

q5.a: Contact us through the app's in-app support feature, call our hotline (available during business hours), or email support@dynamicstransport.com. Our team is here to help.

c1.desc: All matched drivers are notified; the request is removed.

c2.label: Driver Cancels:

c4.desc: Automatic cancellation due to timeout or rule violation.

q1.q: How is the shipping price determined?
q1.a: Prices are determined through competitive bidding. When you post a shipment, drivers submit their proposed prices. You can set a budget or leave it open for drivers to bid freely. Choose the best offer based on price, ratings, and vehicle type.

q2.a: DTC is currently free — no commission is charged. Drivers keep 100% of their earnings during the launch period. We will announce a transparent commission structure before introducing any fees.

q3.q: Are there any hidden fees for shippers?
q3.a: No. Shippers do not pay any platform fees. You only pay the agreed shipping cost to the driver. Driver subscriptions are optional during launch.

q4.a: The bidding system is your negotiation tool. You can review multiple bids and choose the one that fits your budget. If no bids meet your expectations, you can repost with a different budget.

q5.q: What happens if I don't have a subscription?
q5.a: Drivers need an active subscription to receive shipment requests. When your subscription expires, your status changes to 'Inactive - No Subscription' and you won't receive new job notifications until you renew.

BlogPost.title: How to Ship Cargo from Addis Ababa to Djibouti (2026 Guide)
BlogPost.intro: The Addis Ababa–Djibouti corridor is the artery of Ethiopia's trade, carrying roughly 95% of the country's imports and exports. Here's everything you need to ship cargo on it in 2026 — without surprises.

doc.title: Step 1 — Prepare Your Documentation
doc.sub: Before any truck rolls, your cargo needs to clear customs. Have these ready:

d1.title: Customs declaration
d1.text: Filed by your licensed clearing agent against the cargo value and HS code.

d2.title: Commercial invoice
d2.text: Details goods, quantity, value, and the buyer/seller. Keep a copy in the truck.

d3.title: Packing list
d3.text: Weight, dimensions, and contents of each package — used for physical inspection and truck matching.

d4.title: Transit document
d4.text: For containers moving onward to Djibouti Port, confirm the transit declaration (bond) so cargo doesn't sit at the border.

trucks.title: Step 2 — Choose Your Truck Type
trucks.sub: The right vehicle keeps your per-quintal cost low and matches the cargo. Rates quoted per quintal (100 kg).

post.title: Step 3 — Post Your Load & Get Bids
post.text: Post your shipment on the DTC app or website with pickup, destination, weight, and vehicle type. Verified drivers bid on your load — you compare quotes, ratings, and vehicles, then pick the best offer. No platform commission; you pay the driver directly only on delivery.

costs.title: What It Costs
costs.sub: Rates below are typical per-quintal ranges after a competitive bid — posted rates are agreed with the driver, never set by DTC.
costs.footnote: Post a load now to receive exact bids — free during launch, no hidden fees.

f1.q: How long does it take to ship from Addis Ababa to Djibouti?
f1.a: Road freight typically takes 2–3 days, while the Addis Ababa–Djibouti railway (Addis–Djibouti Standard Gauge) moves containers in about 12 hours. Road is more flexible for door-to-door and non-container cargo.

f2.q: What documents do I need to clear cargo in Djibouti?
f2.a: You need a full customs declaration, commercial invoice, packing list, and for many shipments a Certificate of Origin. Registered clearing agents handle the process for you; DTC matches you with verified drivers once loaded.

f3.q: What is the current Djibouti corridor rate?
f3.a: Rates fluctuate with diesel prices and season. Trucks typically charge roughly 3,000–7,000 ETB per quintal depending on vehicle class. Post your load on DTC and get competing bids from verified drivers — rates are agreed with the driver, never set by us.
